Subject: Interleaved timeband plan & next steps — Technical deep dive availability

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Great to meet earlier today — thanks for the intro to the Acme platform and the use cases you walked us through. Quick post-call recap and proposal so we can lock the next step (technical deep dive + demo):

Key points from discovery:
- Primary goal: evaluate Redwood inference runtime for low-latency inference across multi-region production (cost vs latency trade-offs).
- Stakeholders: Sarah (PM), Tom (Platform lead), two SEs who will join the deep dive.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence will be required later; for now sample data pipeline and retention questions noted.

Proposed next step: 60–75 minute technical deep dive + live demo. Because your team spans UK and APAC, we suggest a lightweight rotating schedule so the primary window alternates region-friendly hours each meeting rather than always forcing one timezone. Our suggested "ping-pong" rotation (keeps the primary slot friendly to one region each meeting and rotates every week):

Ping-pong rotation (example):
- Week A (EU-priority): 09:30–10:45 BST / 01:30–02:45 PDT / 17:30–18:45 SGT
- Week B (US-priority): 09:00–10:15 PDT / 17:00–18:15 BST / 00:00–01:15 SGT (next day)
- Week C (APAC-priority): 14:00–15:15 SGT / 23:00–00:15 BST / 15:00–16:15 PDT

Notes on rotation:
- We propose rotating the primary-friendly slot each meeting on a 3-week cycle so no single stakeholder group is always inconvenienced.
- If Tom or others prefer a monthly rotation instead, we can adapt.
- We will record sessions and share the recording / condensed notes after each meeting.

Candidate dates/times we can offer for the first deep dive (we can swap to other dates if needed):
- Thu Oct 2, 09:30 BST (EU-priority sample)
- Tue Oct 7, 09:00 PDT (US-priority sample)
- Wed Oct 15, 14:00 SGT (APAC-priority sample)

Attachments: tech_deep_dive_agenda.pdf (agenda + section owners), acme_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (draft MAP).

Action items / asks:
1) Sarah/Tom — which of the three candidate slots above works best for your team, or share 2–3 alternatives (we can then send a calendar invite).
2) Let us know if you want the session recorded and shared internally (we'llenable recording and post a trimmed highlights clip).
3) Ben / Vivek — if you can host the demo on your side, I will include you as presenters and send the invite after we lock the time.

Thanks — looking forward to the next step.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Quick answers from our side:
- EU mornings are generally easiest for core stakeholders (UK/POL teams). Of your proposed slots, Thu Oct 2 at 09:30 BST looks promising.
- Tom (cc) is our platform lead — he flagged that some of our engineers are on APAC hours and would prefer the APAC-friendly option occasionally; rotating is fine.
- We definitely want the sessions recorded. If you could also share a short pre-read (1 pager) summarizing what the demo will cover (latency numbers, expected throughput, cost levers) that would be great.

Two small constraints:
- We prefer demos that start within the top-of-hour or half-hour marks (no 20/50 start times) — helps our calendar tooling.
- Please avoid repeating deep infra config that references our internal SSO until after we sign an NDA.

For the first session, Tentative: Thu Oct 2, 09:30 BST — Tom and I will confirm formally by EOD Tue Sep 23. If that works, can you seed a calendar invite (we'll convert to a rotating series once we agree cadence)?

Thanks,
